prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2025-10-28. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 0.55 |
| Retained earnings       | 34,747M |
| Current liabilities     | 22,911M |
| Current assets          | 12,671M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 54,181M |
| Total liabilities       | 139,758M |
| Total assets            | 204,354M |
| EBIT / operating income | 2,527M |
| Revenue                 | 7,966M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2025-10-28, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company exhibits a very weak current ratio of 0.55, indicating significant short-term liquidity issues. The high total liabilities relative to total assets (139,758M vs 204,354M) and shareholders' equity (54,181M) suggest a highly leveraged capital structure. While retained earnings are substantial, the low EBIT relative to revenue (2,527M vs 7,966M) points to modest profitability, which may not be sufficient to service the large debt burden.

DECISION: BB-
